title: Tournament pairs in the Listening Room — the first human blind session (Wave Q, Workstream A)
definitionOfDone: a real balanced session, drawn from a real tournament report, rendered to real audio, opened through the real API, served to a real browser, and rated end to end by a real HTTP client. Not a fixture.

session.title: Wave Q blind session 1 - tournament pairs (classical PDMX)
session.source: docs/evidence/model-tournament-live.json (runId 4fac41bee93e, 12 classical PDMX tasks x 3 seeds x 5 arms)
session.primaryQuestion: Overall: which version do you prefer?

blindness.raterViewContains: position, instrument family, two token-addressed audio URLs, the questions
blindness.orientation: A/B side decided per pair by hash of (session, cell); the comparison's first arm is on the left in 22 of 50 pairs
verifiedBy: the tournamentListening suite's leak test over eight rater ids
a live GET of the rater view (all four leak probes false)

votePathProof.note: run on a separate 10-pair smoke session so the owner's 50-pair session stays unrated
votePathProof.rater: a second local identity, not the owner

gateC.reason: 1 independent rater(s) so far; Gate C needs at least 5.

sampleRecord.question: Overall: which version do you prefer?

howAPairSounds: both sides of a pair are the same passage: every context track plus the held-out part written by that arm, rendered by the platform's own REFERENCE_SYNTH_V1 (deterministic, one voice per family), candidate 1.35x forward, peak-normalised to -1 dBFS. Same renderer for the human part and for every model, so a rater compares notes and not sound design.

gatePolicy.onlyGatePairsCount: Gate C reads only the pairs that put the challenger against the incumbent; the other four comparisons inform the decision pack and the reward model
gatePolicy.ownerVotes: recorded, shown apart, excluded from the verdict — the owner is the first rater, not the verdict

rewardModelData: every vote is exported as a preference record (comparison, task, seed, family, both arms in comparison order, both tournament entry keys, winner, loser, salted rater pseudonym) — the shape a pairwise preference loss consumes. GET /api/listening-sessions/<id>/preferences, owner only.
honestLimits: Nobody has rated the 50-pair session yet. The owner is the first rater; Gate C needs five independent raters and a 60 % release share, so one person's session is evidence, not a verdict.
All 50 pairs come from the classical PDMX tournament. The non-classical session waits on that tournament (Workstream B).
The renderer is a deterministic synth, not a sampled orchestra. It is fair across arms and it is not what a producer would ship.
Opening the session took 3 min 18 s for 100 renders (~2 s each, single-threaded, in-process). Fine for 50 pairs, not for thousands.
The smoke session's tallies come from one client alternating A/B on purpose; they say the plumbing works, nothing about quality.
